subject: Question on the Sleep Regularity Index Calculation

messages.author: 7c38f73a4b85d711
messages.subject: Question on the Sleep Regularity Index Calculation
parts:
Hi, 

I am getting some numbers that at a visual glance do not seem to match the visual reports of sleep and the sleep regularity index. I was looking at the code and was wondering, when individuals are considered to have SPT Window: wakefulness (so GGIR considers them awake), would that be computed as 0 for wakefulness when it comes to the sleep regularity index? 

Thank you,
Zachary

messages.subject: Re: Question on the Sleep Regularity Index Calculation
parts:
Hi,

After looking at the code, I think GGIR uses the definition of sleep by g.sib.det, meaning that awake epochs within the SPT are considered to be awake (= 0). However, it would be good if Vincent can confirm this.

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Question on the Sleep Regularity Index Calculation
parts: would that be computed as 0 for wakefulness when it comes to the sleep regularity index?

Yes, that is correct. GGIR currently only uses the sustained inactivity bouts (24 hour rest periods) for SRI detection. I did that because there is no proven method yet for nap detection in the general population. Implementing the original approach would implicitly come with the claim that we can detect naps.

Possibly in the upcoming month I will add the option to smooth these rest periods, such that it is a better approximation of the original method as proposed by Windred.

Best, Vincent
